title: Holistic KV Stripe Prefetch Controller for Fragmented/Paged GPU Residency
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Design and implement a stripe-oriented prefetch controller for the paged/blocked KV cache to reduce tail latency and PCIe thrashing for workloads with highly skewed token hotsets and fragmented residency. The controller coordinates with the continuous batching layer to drive aligned DMA transfers, makes admission decisions at stripe granularity, and conservatively evicts micro-blocks to maintain GPU memory headroom without violating latency SLOs.
background: We currently observe two correlated issues under mixed workloads: (1) frequent small PCIe page swaps caused by non-coalesced host->GPU transfers for fragmented KV hot entries and (2) batch-affine latency spikes when requests miss in the GPU-resident KV and cause synchronous loads. Existing slab allocators operate at a block level but lack a runtime controller that reasons about access skew, batch alignment, and burstiness across tenants. Past tickets (see dependencies) explored block allocators, prefetching prototypes and residency orchestration, but none provide a unified streaming prefetch controller that ties into continuous batching and kernel scheduling.
proposal: Introduce a Holistic KV Stripe Prefetch Controller (HKSPC) with the following capabilities: 1) stripe-level metadata tracking (recently-accessed fingerprint, access rate, estimated next-access time) computed in the host process; 2) batch-aligned prefetch windows: HKSPC queries the batching layer about upcoming sequence lengths and routes to schedule prefetch DMA that overlaps with host CPU scheduling and kernel warmup; 3) adaptive admission: treat consecutive micro-blocks within a stripe as a single admission atom to reduce PCIe scatter; 4) grace-time micro-eviction: allow short in-GPU residency for low-likelihood hot entries that fall outside the immediate hotset; 5) fallback fast-path: if prefetch budget exhausted, HKSPC signals the runtime to use a smaller quantized model variant or per-request streaming fallback to preserve latency SLOs.
technical_spec:
- Metadata: per-stripe ring buffer with (fingerprint, last_access_ts, hit_count, resident_chunks, estimated_bytes). Stored in host memory and periodically synchronized with the runtime.
- Admission policy: score = alpha*hit_rate + beta*(recent_accesses/second) - gamma*resident_bytes; admission if score > dynamic_threshold and host->gpu_bandwidth_budget available.
- Prefetch scheduling: group micro-block reads by contiguous GPU address ranges; use coalesced DMA with max_transfer_size 4MB; align transfers to page-boundaries; schedule to start when batch window >= predicted_load_latency.
- Eviction policy: soft-evict least-score micro-blocks within stripe first; when memory pressure persists, escalate to full-stripe demotion and writeback checkpoints.
- Integrations: API hooks between HKSPC and batching controller: getNextBatchWindow(), notifyBatchCommitted(batch_id), reportKernelWarmupComplete(model_variant). Use telemetry events for decisions to feed Optimize heuristic engine.
implementation_steps: Prototype host-side stripe metadata collector (C++): sample accesses and build per-stripe stats
Add controller service in runtime process (Rust): admission logic, scheduling, policy toggles
Batching layer API extension: expose upcoming batch window and per-request affinity hints
DMA coalescer: implement aggregated H2D transfer path with aligned copy and PCIe pacing
Eviction hooks: integrate micro-eviction + stripe demotion into existing slab allocator
E2E tests and synthetic workloads (see testing_plan)
Perf runbook and dashboard wiring (Telemetry: prefetch_events, admission_rate, pciethroughput, residencystats)
Canary rollout to Dedicated cluster with strict SLO monitoring
testing_plan: Unit tests for admission scoring variants and synthetic stripe traces
Emulated PCIe throttling tests to validate pacing and transfer coalescing
Microbench: tail P99/P999 latency under hotset skew (Zipf alpha sweep) vs baseline
Integration: continuous-batching + prefetch overlap latency regression tests
Fault injection: lost DMA, timed-out transfers, and recovery path verification
A/B experiment on Dedicated with traffic shadowing to measure 95/99 latency, token cost, and PCIe IO patterns
rollout_plan: Feature flagged implementation behind runtime flag `hkspc_enabled`
Internal canary: 5% of Dedicated capacity running hkspc for low-risk tenants
Gradual ramp: increase to 25% after 48h of zero regressions, then 100% for non-sensitive tenants
Enterprise opt-in for Private deployments (requires security review)
Full rollout conditioned on meeting P99 latency and PCIe bandwidth budget targets for two consecutive weeks

decisions: Prefer stripe-granularity admission vs per-microblock to reduce PCIe request count (chosen after simulation trade-offs)
Use host-side metadata rather than embedding in GPU-resident structures to avoid additional GPU memory pressure
Cap single coalesced transfer to 4MB to avoid starving other DMA streams while still getting practical coalescing benefits
tradeoffs: Stripe-level admission increases false-positive prefetches for some workloads (extra PCIe bytes) but reduces small-transfer overhead and cumulative latency for common skewed workloads
Host-side metadata costs more CPU cycles and memory but avoids increasing GPU memory footprint and allows easier rollout in Private deployments
Conservative eviction reduces OOM frequency but can slightly increase token cost when re-fetching evicted micro-blocks
notes: Next: finalize cancellation semantics with batching team; run long-duration canary under multi-tenant noise. Follow-up ticket will add RL-based admission tuner if heuristic plateaus.
